title: Ligating and dividing a vessel on a model

guidelineVersions: RCS England Surgical Care Practitioner Curriculum Framework (2022; accessed 12 October 2026)
RCS England Good Surgical Practice (2025; accessed 12 October 2026)

brief.scenario: You are a core surgical trainee performing a simulated procedure. A model has an isolated, clearly identified small vessel requiring controlled ligation and division. The model contains no live patient.
brief.task: Demonstrate safe exposure, atraumatic clamping, secure proximal and distal control, ligation, division and haemostasis. Explain what changes if the structure cannot confidently be identified, and respond to simulated bleeding.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Tests disciplined identification and vascular control before cutting; the model is a means of assessing judgement as well as manual skill.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Dividing a presumed vessel after a single loose tie without securing both sides or checking neighbouring structures.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: “Before I clamp anything, I will expose the structure and confirm what it is and what lies behind it.”

flow: Orient and expose vessel and surrounding structures; assess safe identification.
Select instruments and place controlled clamps without unnecessary crush.
Apply secure ligatures to both sides (transfix if appropriate to the model/diameter).
Divide only between secured controls, protecting adjacent tissues.
Release/check deliberately for bleeding, handle failure and document safe completion.

grid.label: Identification and anatomy
grid.borderline: Names vessel but fails to assess surrounding anatomy.
grid.pass: Confirms vessel and adjacent structures before control.
grid.high: States decision to stop if identity or relation is uncertain.

grid.label: Preparation and communication
grid.pass: Checks instruments, model, working space and communicates plan.
grid.high: Anticipates clamp sizes and second control before first action.

grid.label: Exposure and handling
grid.fail: Traction tears model or catches neighbours.
grid.pass: Uses gentle traction and adequate visualisation.
grid.high: Retracts tissues to expose both ends while avoiding injury.

grid.label: Proximal control
grid.borderline: Clamp slips or is poorly oriented.
grid.pass: Controls proximal side with appropriate atraumatic clamp.
grid.high: Demonstrates stable placement with minimal collateral tissue.

grid.label: Distal control
grid.high: Anticipates back-bleeding and verifies both controls.

grid.label: Ligature and knot
grid.fail: Knot loose or only one side tied.
grid.pass: Correct suture choice for model; secure knot and appropriate placement.
grid.high: Checks knot seating, security and need for transfixion in a larger/slippery pedicle.

grid.label: Safe division
grid.pass: Divides clearly between secure ligatures away from adjacent structures.
grid.high: Controlled instrument orientation with deliberate distance from ties.

grid.label: Haemostasis and rescue
grid.pass: Checks both stumps and uses direct pressure/re-control if simulated bleeding occurs.
grid.high: Calls senior help early for uncontrolled bleeding; does not blindly clamp unseen tissue.

grid.label: Completion and professionalism
grid.pass: Confirms haemostasis, safe sharps and clear handover.
grid.high: Explains limitations of model and how real bleeding would trigger structured escalation.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It looks like a vessel; I will cut it now.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I have not looked. It should be fine.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I do not need to check the instruments or tell anyone my plan; I will just start.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Pulls hard on the model, leaving the posterior structure obscured.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Places one clamp with the tip partly outside the visible field.]

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Do you need control on the other side?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Not really; one side is enough.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Places a loose single throw proximal to the clamp.] That will hold.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Would you cut now if you were not certain this was a vessel?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Yes; we can find out once divided.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: There is no point checking. We have finished.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: A proximal stump is now leaking on the model.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will clamp whatever is nearest without looking.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Leaves loose sharp instrument at the edge.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will inspect the full exposed length and identify what is adjacent before placing any clamp. Is there anything important behind this vessel?

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: There is a fragile structure just behind it.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will carefully lift the vessel into view without traction on the posterior structure, using a safe plane.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I have a suitable clamp on each side, a ligature and scissors ready. My plan is two-sided control, secure ties and division between them.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Positions an atraumatic proximal clamp across the model vessel.] I can see the clamp tip and that the posterior structure is clear.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Places distal clamp under vision.] Both sides are now controlled.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Would you cut now if you were not certain this was a vessel?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No. I would stop, improve exposure and ask my senior to confirm the anatomy before making an irreversible cut.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Places and securely seats proximal and distal ligatures, checking that they do not slip.] On a larger or slippery pedicle I would assess the need for transfixion.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Divides between secure ties, keeping scissors away from adjacent tissue and knot tails.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I am checking both stumps for bleeding before declaring haemostasis.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: A small proximal leak is now simulated.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would maintain visual control, apply direct pressure, then place an additional secure ligature after identifying the exact leak. If I cannot control it promptly I would call for senior help.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Checks both ends and sharps.] I would document what was ligated and any complication in a real operation.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Before this irreversible step I want unambiguous identification. I will trace this model structure in both directions and identify what is immediately posterior to it. Is the adjacent anatomy visible?

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: There is a fragile posterior structure.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Repositions retraction, isolates the vessel without crushing it and keeps the neighbouring structure in sight.] I have a view that will let me see clamp tips and both future stumps.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I have matched clamp size to the model and prepared ties before any division; my assistant would be briefed to maintain exposure rather than traction on the nearby structure.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Places proximal clamp at a stable point without including extra tissue.] I can see the full jaw and control position.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Controls the distal side independently and gently tests stability.] I am guarding against both forward bleeding and back-bleeding.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Would you divide if uncertain whether it was the intended vessel?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Absolutely not. I would reassess landmarks, obtain additional exposure and request senior verification; the technical skill cannot justify a wrong-structure injury.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Places evenly tensioned secure ligatures beyond both clamp positions.] I will inspect knot seating rather than assuming the throw count guarantees security. If this were a larger vessel I would reassess whether transfixion or another vascular control method was appropriate.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Divides centrally between ties with only the required scissor movement.] The adjacent structure remains protected.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Inspects proximal and distal stumps in turn.] I will only release control in a manner that lets me identify any leak immediately.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: A little proximal bleeding appears on the model.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will compress the visible source, keep the field clear and resecure that stump under direct vision. If bleeding persists or the anatomy becomes obscured, stop blind manoeuvres and escalate immediately.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Checks final model haemostasis and secures sharps.] In a real operation I would communicate the vessel divided, technique, blood loss and concerns to the team and record it accurately.

failures.move: Dividing a structure whose identity is uncertain.
failures.consequence: May sever a nerve, duct or major vessel.

failures.move: Relying on a visibly insecure single loose tie.

recovery.when: If you cannot safely see the far clamp tip
recovery.line: I cannot safely see the far clamp tip; I will stop and improve exposure before any division.
The stump is leaking; I will control it under vision, resecure it and ask for senior help if it persists.

knowledge.fact: The RCS England curriculum framework for surgical care practitioners includes knot tying and assisting with haemostasis among its technical skills.
Clamp and divide only after confident identification of the structure and its neighbours; do not cut an uncertain structure.
Knot security and controlled suturing/ligation are technical competencies, not a prescribed national number of throws.
Bleeding needs directed, visualised control; blind clamping risks injuring unseen structures.
A model demonstration does not establish competence on a live patient; supervised progression is essential.

recall.think: Can I positively identify this structure and its neighbours?
recall.say: “Both sides controlled; I will divide only under direct vision.”
do: Expose, clamp both sides, ligate securely, divide safely.

numbers.meaning: No universal tie-throw count or numerical threshold in the cited RCS standards.

recall.trap: A neat knot does not compensate for cutting the wrong structure.
recall.finish: Inspect both stumps and account for instruments.

partner.opening: Please ligate and divide this identified model vessel.

reveals.finding: the vessel is visible but there is a fragile adjacent structure posteriorly.

reveals.trigger: During the haemostasis check, only if the candidate looks for bleeding
reveals.finding: Simulate a small leak from the proximal stump.

push.question: After both controls are placed, ask: “Would you cut now if you were not certain this was a vessel?”
